question: The coal that we use now comes from plants that lived around _________ years ago
solution:
The correct answer is __**10,000,000 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The coal we use today was formed from plants that existed around **10 million to 300 million years ago**.
 
• These plants were primarily large ferns, trees, and other vegetation that thrived in swampy environments.
 
• Over millions of years, these plants were buried under layers of water and dirt, compressing them into peat and eventually into coal.
 
• Coal formation is a process that involves the accumulation of plant debris in a swampy environment, followed by burial and compaction.
 
• This process requires millions of years of geological time to transform plant material into coal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Coal**

 
 
• There are four main types of coal: **anthracite, bituminous, sub-bituminous, and lignite.**
 
• Anthracite has the highest carbon content and energy density, while lignite has the lowest.
 
 
 
• **Coal Formation Stages**
 
 
• The stages of coal formation include peat, lignite, sub-bituminous, bituminous, and anthracite.
 
• Each stage represents a different level of compression and heat applied over millions of years.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Coal**
 
 
• Coal is primarily used as a fuel for electricity generation.
 
• It is also used in the production of steel and cement.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact**
 
 
• Coal mining and burning contribute to air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions.
 
• Efforts are being made to reduce the environmental impact through cleaner coal technologies and alternative energy sources.
